question: Can a neural model discover lower-dimensional macrostates from observational dynamics whose dimension-normalized effective information exceeds that of the original system?

key_findings.claim: NIS+ searches jointly for a coarse-graining map, macro dynamics, and an approximate inverse while maximizing dimension-averaged effective information subject to a normalized prediction-error threshold.
key_findings.evidence: The objective rewrites interventional effective information as a reweighted inverse-dynamics likelihood, uses density estimation to approximate a uniform intervention distribution, and accepts an emergence score only when normalized MAE is below 0.3.

key_findings.claim: On the synthetic SIR system, the learned two-dimensional macrostate gives more accurate multi-step and out-of-distribution dynamics than parameter-matched neural and autoencoder baselines while yielding positive causal emergence over a range of noise levels.
key_findings.evidence: The experiments train on 63,000 complete or 42,000 partially observed transitions, evaluate 10-step forecasts and a held-out triangular region, and compare NIS+, NIS, NN/NN+, and VAE/VAE+ with approximately matched parameter counts.

key_findings.claim: In the boids benchmark, eight learned macro dimensions separate two artificially defined flocks and support longer-horizon prediction, with intrinsic and observation noise producing different trends in the reported emergence score.
key_findings.evidence: The benchmark splits 16 boids into two groups with distinct turning forces; information-gradient attributions associate latent components with the groups, and 50-step/OOD plots compare NIS+ against NIS as noise is varied.

key_findings.claim: The fMRI results do not establish an experimentally intervenable one-dimensional brain cause: the highest-emergence movie-watching representation is selected from shared stimulus-locked observational dynamics, and a better-predicting 27-dimensional model has negative emergence.
key_findings.evidence: The analysis reduces Schaefer-parcellated signals to 100 regions for 830 subjects watching the same clip, reports maximum emergence at q=1, and separately notes that q=27 improves long-rollout prediction but produces a negative emergence value attributed to overfitting.

anchors.section: Section 4.4, fMRI data and dimensional sweep

key_findings.claim: The reported quantity is causal only relative to the learned Markov model and a constructed uniform intervention distribution; no physical interventions identify the macrostate or rule out observational confounding.
key_findings.evidence: The method estimates observational densities with KDE, reweights samples to emulate do-interventions, assumes a fully observed Markov transition, and lists hidden variables and non-Markovian systems as outside scope.

method.core_idea: Optimize a learned coarse-graining for effective information per retained dimension while requiring that the macrostate remains dynamically predictive.
method.mechanism: An invertible RealNVP encoder transforms the microstate, a projection retains q macro coordinates, a decoder reconstructs dropped coordinates with Gaussian auxiliaries, and learned forward and reverse transition networks estimate predictive error and intervention-reweighted effective information. The method searches q and reports the difference between macro and micro dimension-averaged information.
assumptions: Observed transitions are sufficiently sampled from a stationary, fully observed Markov process.
A homogeneous global coarse-graining and macro transition model are meaningful over the sampled state space.
Kernel density estimates and importance weights adequately approximate a uniform macro intervention distribution.
Normalized prediction error below 0.3 is an adequate safeguard against spurious information maximization.

techniques.role: Learns an invertible coordinate system before retaining q macro dimensions.
Reweights observational transitions toward an idealized uniform intervention distribution.
Turns the effective-information objective into a trainable inverse-prediction likelihood.
Attributes macro information to micro variables for qualitative interpretation.

evaluations.setting: Noisy SIR dynamics with full and partial observation
evaluations.metric: Ten-step error, OOD error, and dimension-averaged causal emergence
evaluations.result: A q=2 NIS+ representation is reported to outperform parameter-matched NN, VAE, and non-information-maximizing variants on prediction while retaining positive emergence under admissible error.
evaluations.baseline: NIS, NN/NN+, VAE/VAE+, and the Rosas et al. emergence measure

evaluations.setting: Sixteen-boid dynamics split into two rule-defined groups
evaluations.metric: Fifty-step and OOD prediction, emergence across noise, information-gradient attribution
evaluations.result: The selected q=8 representation tracks the two groups and improves long-horizon/OOD prediction; intrinsic rule noise lowers emergence whereas added observation noise can raise it below the error cutoff.

evaluations.setting: AOMIC ID1000 movie-watching and resting-state fMRI
evaluations.metric: Prediction error and causal-emergence score over latent dimension q
evaluations.result: The movie data maximize the score at q=1 and the rest data at q=7; the better-predicting q=27 movie model has negative emergence and neither result receives interventional neuroscientific validation.
evaluations.baseline: Micro dynamics and alternative latent dimensions

evaluations.result: The method recovers compact features associated with higher-level configurations in a canonical discrete cellular system.
evaluations.baseline: Microstate dynamics and the earlier NIS framework

limitations: Reliable density reweighting and inverse dynamics require large, representative transition datasets.
The prediction-error threshold of 0.3 is heuristic, and insufficient training can create false emergence.
The learned neural macro dynamics and coarse variables can remain difficult to interpret.
The framework is global and Markovian and does not model hidden state, history dependence, or locally varying macroscales.
Real-data evidence is observational and does not validate claimed causal macrostates through interventions or downstream scientific predictions.
failure_modes: Importance weights explode where the observational density has weak support relative to the synthetic intervention distribution.
A flexible reverse model can inflate the objective by exploiting finite-sample density artifacts.
Searching latent dimension on the same data can select an unstable or overfit emergence maximum.
Shared exogenous drivers, such as a common movie stimulus, can be encoded as a macrostate and misread as intrinsic causal organization.
A low-error small benchmark need not preserve the ordering of representations at larger state dimension or different noise regimes.
reusable_insights: Treat causal-emergence discovery as a multi-objective problem: intervention validity, dynamics accuracy, compression, and stability should be audited separately.
Report effective sample size and support overlap for any observational-to-interventional reweighting scheme.
Validate learned macrostates with held-out interventions or novel-condition forecasts, not only reconstruction and rollout error.
Repeat the latent-dimension search across seeds, samples, and model classes to distinguish stable emergence from selection noise.
open_questions: Can causal macrostates be identified under partial observability without assuming a first-order Markov microstate?
Which intervention distributions are scientifically meaningful for continuous biological and social systems?
How should uncertainty in density estimation and reverse dynamics propagate into an emergence score?
Do the selected dimensions and information attributions remain stable under equivalent state reparameterizations?
Can an independently designed intervention falsify the one-dimensional fMRI macrostate?

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Information Squeezer for Causal Emergence
competitive_landscape.difference: NIS already learns coarse-graining and macro dynamics from time series; NIS+ adds explicit dimension-averaged effective-information maximization and inverse-dynamics/density-reweighting machinery.

competitive_landscape.title: Reconciling emergences: An information-theoretic approach to identify causal emergence in multivariate data
competitive_landscape.difference: Rosas et al. define downward causation and causal decoupling using multivariate information decomposition; NIS+ searches neural coarse-grainings using effective information and a learned intervention model.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal emergence is widespread across measures of causation
competitive_landscape.difference: Comolatti and Hoel establish examples across many causal measures; NIS+ provides an optimization pipeline for continuous observational dynamics but rests on one chosen normalized effective-information objective.

competitive_landscape.title: SVD-based Causal Emergence for Gaussian Iterative Systems
competitive_landscape.difference: The SVD method derives coarse-grainings from forward/backward covariance spectra for Gaussian iterative systems; NIS+ is more flexible and nonlinear but relies on neural optimization, KDE, and a heuristic error constraint.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: NIS+ is a general neural framework that directly maximizes effective information to discover causal emergence and interpretable macrostates from high-dimensional time series.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper derives a trainable intervention-reweighted inverse-dynamics objective and applies one implementation across SIR, boids, Game of Life, and fMRI.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The objective-level extension over NIS and breadth of demonstrations are substantive, but the causal interpretation is model-relative: observational reweighting, Markov sufficiency, density support, and a heuristic accuracy threshold are not substitutes for real interventions.
